mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY growth exceeds 2.5% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over the previous 3 months signals strengthening demand, boosting economic sentiment and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases by more than 5% in 3 months and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% over the previous 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5% in 3 months and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the previous 3 months signals increased economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases by more than 1% in 3 months and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy, which reduces borrowing costs and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS decreases and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than industrial production (INDPRO) over the previous 3 months, it signals a demand-driven expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > INDPRO growth in 3 months
failure_condition: If RSAFS growth exceeds INDPRO growth in 3 months and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% over the previous 3 months, it signals a strong labor market, boosting economic sentiment and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 3 months
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.3% in 3 months, and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is below 2% YoY, it signals a restrictive monetary policy in a low-growth environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: restrictive monetary policy in low-growth environment
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is above 4% and GDPC1 YoY growth is below 2%, and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.
